name: Fabric Loom
capability: Gradle workspace setup, Minecraft dependency provisioning, decompilation, remapping, access widener migration, run configurations, production runs and game-test integration.
bestFor: Fabric source ports, namespace migration and reproducible target builds.
integration: Generate version-pinned workspaces and invoke mapping migration, remapJar, runClient, runServer and production test tasks inside isolated build sandboxes.
currentEvidence: Loom 1.16 is the latest stable release observed on 2026-08-20; active 1.17 development builds are already used for Minecraft 26.2.
risks: Build scripts are version-sensitive
New unobfuscated Minecraft versions use different plugin/remapping paths

name: Fabric Loader
capability: Mostly version-independent Fabric loader, metadata validation, dependency resolution and entrypoint discovery.
bestFor: Exact Fabric runtime contract validation and clean target profiles.
integration: Resolve supported loader versions from Fabric Meta, validate fabric.mod.json and launch clean compatibility matrices.
currentEvidence: Actively maintained through July 2026.

name: Fabric API
capability: Core event, registry, networking, rendering, lifecycle and game-test APIs used by a large share of Fabric mods.
bestFor: Determining whether a Fabric port depends on loader-only APIs or Fabric API modules.
integration: Map module-level dependencies, detect API removals and run version-specific compile/runtime tests.
currentEvidence: Actively maintained for current Minecraft releases.

name: Fabric Documentation
capability: Official build, mappings, data generation, networking, rendering and migration documentation.
bestFor: Version-correct source transformations and explanation links in repair plans.
integration: Index versioned migration pages and attach the exact relevant documentation to generated actions.

name: Mapping IO
capability: Read, write, transform and compose mapping formats and namespaces.
bestFor: Building source-to-target mapping graphs across official, intermediary, Yarn and custom mappings.
integration: Normalize every mapping source into one graph, retain provenance and reject unresolved or ambiguous symbols.

name: Tiny Remapper
capability: Fast Java bytecode remapping with hierarchy-aware member resolution and extension points.
bestFor: Rewriting compiled mod JAR namespaces and class/member references before deeper API repair.
integration: Perform deterministic dry-run remaps, capture unresolved references, compare class trees and preserve reproducible inputs.

name: Yarn Mappings
capability: Community-readable names and documentation for Minecraft classes, fields and methods.
bestFor: Human-understandable Fabric source reconstruction and cross-version symbol comparison.
integration: Version-pin mappings and retain official/intermediary/Yarn namespace correspondences in the porting graph.
risks: Mapping names can change independently of behavior

name: Fabric Intermediary
capability: Stable intermediary namespace traditionally used to keep Fabric mods portable across obfuscated releases.
bestFor: Cross-version identity and binary remapping for pre-26.1 Minecraft releases.
integration: Use as one mapping edge for legacy versions; bypass where post-26.1 unobfuscated builds make it unnecessary.
risks: Post-26.1 unobfuscated Minecraft changes the need for intermediary remapping

name: Enigma
capability: Interactive deobfuscation and mapping editor with source/class views.
bestFor: Resolving ambiguous decompiler output and authoring missing mappings during closed-source reconstruction.
integration: Open only unresolved symbol clusters and export reviewed mappings back into the project mapping graph.

name: Vineflower
capability: Modern Java decompiler derived from Fernflower with strong support for current bytecode constructs.
bestFor: Primary reproducible decompilation of closed-source Minecraft mods.
integration: Decompile with pinned options, retain line maps and compare output against a second decompiler where constructs are ambiguous.
currentEvidence: Version 1.12.0 was the latest release observed during the 2026-08-20 research pass.

name: CFR
capability: Independent Java decompiler with different reconstruction heuristics from Vineflower.
bestFor: Cross-checking switches, lambdas, generics, exception flow and synthetic constructs.
integration: Run as a disagreement detector rather than blindly selecting one decompiler output.

name: ParchmentMC Mappings
capability: Parameter names and community documentation layered over official Mojang mappings.
bestFor: Readable Forge/NeoForge migrations and method-signature intent recovery.
integration: Add a versioned documentation layer to official mappings and preserve its source/version in every generated transform.

name: NeoForge ModDevGradle
capability: Modern NeoForge development plugin with run configurations, configuration-cache support and current Gradle practices.
bestFor: NeoForge source ports and target runtime matrices.
integration: Generate version-pinned NeoForge workspaces, run client/server/data/game-test targets and capture produced artifacts and logs.

name: NeoGradle
capability: NeoForge Gradle toolchain used by supported NeoForge development templates.
bestFor: Projects whose target version or upstream source expects NeoGradle rather than ModDevGradle.
integration: Select from project/target compatibility evidence and avoid gratuitous build-system migration.

name: NeoForge Version Primers
capability: Official change guides describing Java, mappings, registry, rendering, networking, data and API changes between Minecraft versions.
bestFor: Recipe-backed upgrades and downgrades across major Minecraft API transitions.
integration: Convert each primer delta into testable migration rules while retaining the original source link and target range.
currentEvidence: The 1.21.11 to 26.1 primer documents Java 25 and the return to unobfuscated game executables.

name: ForgeGradle
capability: MinecraftForge development, mappings, reobfuscation and run-configuration toolchain.
bestFor: Forge source ports and faithful rebuilding of Forge-origin projects.
integration: Generate target Forge workspaces, preserve access transformers and test client/server/data/game-test runs.

name: MinecraftForge Documentation
capability: Official Forge metadata, registries, events, networking, resources and lifecycle documentation.
bestFor: Validating Forge-specific source and metadata migrations.
integration: Link exact documentation sections to generated findings and code transformations.

name: Quilt Loader
capability: Fabric-compatible loader with Quilt metadata and loader-specific dependency semantics.
bestFor: Quilt-native target validation and Fabric-on-Quilt compatibility testing.
integration: Validate quilt.mod.json, dependency groups and Fabric compatibility in isolated target profiles.
currentEvidence: Quilt announced its non-obfuscated-era direction in February 2026.

name: Architectury Loom
capability: Loom-derived Gradle plugin supporting Fabric, Forge, NeoForge and Quilt development workflows.
bestFor: Multi-loader projects that benefit from shared source and loader-specific outputs.
integration: Use only when a shared-source architecture reduces duplicated behavior without hiding loader-specific correctness.

name: Architectury API and Plugin
capability: Cross-loader abstractions, common-source transforms and loader-specific project structure.
bestFor: Maintaining one source base across supported loaders when the abstraction covers the required APIs.
integration: Generate common and loader-specific modules, then verify each produced artifact independently.
risks: Abstractions do not eliminate loader-specific behavior or testing

name: Modstitch
capability: Unifies official Loom and ModDevGradle workflows and translates access wideners/access transformers for multi-loader projects.
bestFor: Modern Fabric/NeoForge shared-source ports needing loader-native toolchains.
integration: Evaluate as the high-capability shared-build path; retain generated loader-native outputs and independent runtime proof.
risks: Fast-moving build integration requires version pinning and regression tests

name: Stonecutter
capability: Preprocessor and Gradle workflow for maintaining source variants across many Minecraft versions.
bestFor: One mod that must build old and new Minecraft targets without cloning the entire codebase.
integration: Generate explicit version branches/conditions, compile every supported target in CI and reject dead conditional paths.

name: Jared's MultiLoader Template
capability: Practical common-source project template for Fabric, Forge and NeoForge without a required third-party runtime library.
bestFor: Bootstrapping source ports that need transparent loader modules and shared logic.
integration: Use as a generated starting topology, then transplant only verified project behavior and version-specific APIs.

name: Porting Lib
capability: Forge-inspired utilities and compatibility abstractions for Fabric.
bestFor: Reducing repeated Forge-to-Fabric rewrites when the needed subsystem is already implemented.
integration: Select subsystem-by-subsystem and verify API/version support instead of treating it as a universal Forge compatibility layer.

name: OpenRewrite
capability: Loss-minimizing Java source transformation recipes with type attribution and repeatable Gradle/Maven integration.
bestFor: Automating known package, symbol, signature and build migrations while keeping diffs reviewable.
integration: Maintain Minecraft-versioned recipes, apply in dry-run mode, compile after each recipe group and retain provenance for every edit.

name: SpongePowered Mixin
capability: Declarative runtime bytecode injections used throughout the Minecraft mod ecosystem.
bestFor: Inspecting, remapping and repairing injection targets, accessors, invokers and overwrite conflicts.
integration: Parse configs and annotations, resolve exact target bytecode, run audit/export and compare transformed classes in every runtime matrix.

name: MixinExtras
capability: Additional expressive and safer injection primitives layered onto Mixin.
bestFor: Replacing brittle redirects or local-capture patterns during a source port.
integration: Detect bundled/runtime versions and only rewrite injections when target semantics and loader packaging are verified.

name: OW2 ASM
capability: Low-level JVM class parsing, verification, transformation and analysis.
bestFor: Deterministic class structure inspection, descriptor changes, reference graphs and narrowly proven bytecode patches.
integration: Use structured visitors instead of raw string replacement, run CheckClassAdapter and compare intended class-level changes.

name: Recaf
capability: Modern bytecode/source workspace, decompilers, assemblers, scripting/API and headless operations.
bestFor: Interactive investigation and scripted narrow repairs of closed-source JARs.
integration: Use a pinned headless/scripted path for reproducibility; preserve originals and emit entry-level diffs and verification reports.

name: Byte Buddy
capability: High-level Java bytecode generation and runtime instrumentation.
bestFor: Building compatibility shims and controlled adapters when direct JAR mutation is too brittle.
integration: Generate explicit adapters with tests and class-loader constraints; avoid opaque runtime magic.

name: japicmp
capability: Binary compatibility comparison between Java archives.
bestFor: Proving removed/changed classes, methods, fields, descriptors and inheritance across mod or dependency versions.
integration: Compare exact old/new dependency JARs and feed break records into source or bytecode repair planning.

name: Revapi
capability: Extensible API analysis across Java archives with configurable compatibility rules.
bestFor: Maintaining compatibility baselines and detecting accidental API regressions in rebuilt mods.
integration: Run before and after ports, classify intentional changes and block unexplained public API drift.

name: ClassGraph
capability: Fast classpath/module scanning, annotation discovery and dependency metadata inspection.
bestFor: Duplicate classes, shaded libraries, entrypoints and cross-JAR ownership maps.
integration: Build a complete class ownership index and retain collisions as first-class compatibility findings.

name: Sinytra Connector
capability: Runs many Fabric mods on NeoForge through translation and compatibility layers.
bestFor: A controlled temporary or permanent runtime path where the exact mod graph is supported.
integration: Probe exact combinations in isolated profiles, capture incompatibilities and keep source-port plans for unsupported behavior.
currentEvidence: 1.21.1 is the primary supported line; 1.20.1 receives long-term critical fixes.
risks: Not every Fabric API or mixin pattern is compatible
Bridge success is not equivalent to a converted mod

name: Forgified Fabric API
capability: NeoForge-side implementation/port of Fabric API needed by Connector workflows.
bestFor: Fabric API-dependent mods running through Connector.
integration: Resolve exact Connector-compatible versions and test only the modules required by the target graph.

name: Connector Extras
capability: Additional compatibility bridges for selected APIs and mod integrations around Sinytra Connector.
bestFor: Known gaps such as config/menu, recipe viewer or energy/API interoperability covered by a released module.
integration: Select explicit modules from detected dependencies and keep each as an auditable compatibility decision.

name: Kilt
capability: Attempts to run Forge/NeoForge mods on Fabric.
bestFor: Research and isolated compatibility probes when a source port is not yet available.
integration: Never apply automatically to a real profile. Clone the instance, test world safety, collect exact incompatibilities and preserve a source-port fallback.
currentEvidence: Current releases remain explicitly experimental.
risks: May crash or corrupt worlds
Coverage varies sharply by mod and Forge API surface

name: Sinytra Adapter
capability: Sinytra research tooling for adapting incompatible mod behavior and transformations.
bestFor: Harvesting repeatable compatibility patches discovered by Connector analysis.
integration: Evaluate as a compatibility-rule source; import only rules that pass exact artifact/runtime regression tests.

name: Sinytra Probe
capability: Inspection and probing utilities in the Sinytra compatibility ecosystem.
bestFor: Collecting unsupported symbols and translation gaps from runtime-bridge failures.
integration: Normalize findings into the Vault's compatibility knowledge graph and link them to exact versions.

name: packwiz
capability: Declarative, version-controlled modpack management with Modrinth/CurseForge metadata and refresh/update workflows.
bestFor: Reproducible dependency manifests, pack upgrades and rollback-friendly instance composition.
integration: Import/export manifests, reuse CurseForge fingerprint logic, solve provider metadata and verify final pack state.

name: Ferium
capability: CLI mod manager for upgrading projects from Modrinth, CurseForge and GitHub releases.
bestFor: A comparative implementation and command-line fallback for straightforward provider updates.
integration: Benchmark identity/update behavior and borrow only proven provider-resolution ideas while retaining the Vault's deeper repair stages.

name: Modrinth API
capability: Project/version search, exact hash lookup, update lookup, dependency metadata and package downloads.
bestFor: Exact SHA identity, compatible release resolution and dependency staging.
integration: Use SHA-512 identity first, cache versioned metadata, verify published hashes/size and preserve source/project lineage.

name: CurseForge API
capability: Project/file search, fingerprint matching, dependency metadata and downloads where permitted by project distribution settings.
bestFor: Exact MurmurHash2 identity and target-file resolution for CurseForge-hosted mods.
integration: Use authenticated exact fingerprints, verify file/game/loader relations and retain required-dependency changes for explicit review.

name: GitHub API and Releases
capability: Source discovery, tags, commits, release assets, checksums, issues, pull requests and CI evidence.
bestFor: Resolving canonical source and ports not represented by Modrinth or CurseForge.
integration: Require explicit repository identity and target-version/loader evidence before treating an asset as an update.

name: mclo.gs and mclogs API
capability: Minecraft log parsing, paste hosting and structured analyzer integrations.
bestFor: Turning fresh launch logs into normalized failure signatures and shareable evidence.
integration: Keep local/private analysis primary; optionally use structured analyzer rules and preserve exact source lines in repair records.

name: spark
capability: Minecraft profiler for CPU, memory, tick, heap and server/client performance investigations.
bestFor: Performance repair after correctness and compatibility are established.
integration: Capture comparable before/after workloads and reject fixes that merely reduce content or fidelity.

name: Fabric GameTest
capability: Automated in-game tests integrated with Fabric API/Loom.
bestFor: Repeatable behavior verification across Fabric versions and loader targets.
integration: Generate tests from known repair reproducers and run them in target CI/runtime matrices.

name: NeoForge Game Tests
capability: GameTest framework integration and dedicated run targets for NeoForge mods.
bestFor: Behavioral regression proof for NeoForge ports and compatibility patches.
integration: Run server/client-relevant tests plus clean dedicated-server startup before packaging.

name: Gradle Java Toolchains
capability: Reproducible JDK selection, download and compile/test/runtime separation.
bestFor: Building old and new Minecraft targets with their exact Java requirements.
integration: Declare target JDKs per version, compile with release constraints and record vendor/version in build receipts.

name: Minecraft Wiki Technical Documentation
capability: Detailed version history, data/resource pack formats, NBT, registries, commands, world data and technical mechanics.
bestFor: Data-only migrations and cross-checking version-specific schema changes.
integration: Use alongside official release notes and loader primers; store exact page/revision access dates for migration rules.

name: Minecraft Development for IntelliJ
capability: IDE inspections, project generation and support for major Minecraft mod/plugin ecosystems.
bestFor: Human review of generated workspaces, mappings, mixins and metadata.
integration: Optional review environment, not a headless correctness oracle; CI remains authoritative.

name: ModForge
capability: Deterministic class/member migration across Minecraft versions using real mappings and target JAR verification, API deltas, Gradle migration, Mixin checks and an MCP server.
bestFor: Source ports where false-positive renames are more dangerous than explicit unresolved findings.
integration: Run bridge/delta/mixin-check in a copied source workspace; auto-apply only EXACT findings, preserve CANDIDATE and UNRESOLVED evidence, and expose its MCP tools to the porting agent.
currentEvidence: Observed v0.1.2 with current 2026 work, Node 24+, deterministic audit chains and a 170-test suite.
risks: Semantic API redesigns are not automatically solved
Current strongest lane centers on the 1.21.x to 26.x naming boundary
Requires target artifacts and a warmed verified cache for offline operation

name: ModLens MCP
capability: Persistent mod/JAR metadata, class, member, dependency, Mixin, AT/AW and decompiled-source indexing with CLI and MCP access, cross-mod queries, diffs and crash analysis.
bestFor: Giving the Vault and coding agents a searchable local corpus of the exact mods and Minecraft sources being repaired.
integration: Use embedded SQLite by default; ingest exact JARs by hash, call scoped CLI/MCP actions from Doctor reports, and keep the Vault as the authority for mutation/rollback.
currentEvidence: Active through 2026-08-16; recent work includes Node 26 support, SQLite template repair, crash facts and remote modpack ingestion.
risks: Large MCP tool schemas consume context unless profiles disable unused tools
Optional semantic search adds Ollama and database complexity
External decompiler/indexer downloads must be hash-pinned

name: MC Mod Porter
capability: Version-chain rules, build.gradle/gradle.properties/metadata rewrites, Java source patches, resource migrations, build attempts, static debugging and visual testing helpers.
bestFor: Bootstrapping adjacent-version source ports and harvesting verified migration recipes.
integration: Run only on a copied source project, ingest its verified rule corpus, compare every edit, then compile and exercise the actual mod.
currentEvidence: Observed beta 1.1.3 with active July/August 2026 commits and version-chain migration work through 26.2.
risks: Known-pattern rewriting cannot prove semantic equivalence
Third-party mod APIs and major logic redesigns remain manual
Input must be a source project, not a compiled JAR

name: Retromod
capability: Transforms older mod bytecode, mappings, Mixins, access wideners/transformers, metadata, nested JARs and selected runtime contracts for newer Minecraft hosts.
bestFor: Binary-only simple content, library and quality-of-life mods when a source port is unavailable.
integration: Use its standalone CLI in a sandbox, require a compatibility-database match, compare every changed entry, and then launch a copied client/server profile.
currentEvidence: Stable 1.2.0 is the current verified release; the project documents older-mod transformation for modern hosts including current 26.x targets.
risks: Renderer, loader-internal and save-affecting mods may require real source ports
Broad runtime transformation claims demand tuple-specific verification
Never apply directly to the only copy of a modpack or world

name: Crash Assistant
capability: Collects game, launcher and JVM crash artifacts, analyzes known causes, routes reports, identifies environment problems and performs selected common fixes.
bestFor: Reliable end-user crash intake and expanding the Vault signature/remediation corpus.
integration: Import only evidence-backed signatures and fixes into the Repair Brain; keep complete logs and the earliest causal chain.
currentEvidence: Actively maintained multi-branch Fabric/Forge/NeoForge project with shared app/config code and version-specific shims.
risks: A matched warning is not necessarily the terminal root cause
Auto-fixes must remain reversible and version-gated

name: Unimined
capability: Multi-loader, multi-version and legacy-aware Gradle provisioning, mappings, remapping, runs and custom transformation pipelines.
bestFor: Reconstructing and testing modern or legacy source workspaces with one extensible toolchain.
integration: Generate a clean target workspace from the current LTS branch, pin every loader/mapping version, and compare output against loader-native builds.
currentEvidence: Repository default branch observed as lts/1.4 on 2026-08-20.
risks: Very broad support matrix has uneven maturity
Custom/legacy combinations need exact fixture projects and runtime tests

name: Multisource
capability: Gradle settings plugin that models common and loader-specific source sets through feature variants and delegated Architectury Loom projects.
bestFor: Low-duplication Fabric/NeoForge source ownership with explicit parent source sets.
integration: Evaluate in a generated sample, verify remap/publishing artifacts and compare against established Architectury/Stonecutter layouts.
currentEvidence: Repository and plugin documentation available in 2026; adoption remains small.
risks: Limited adoption and release history
Not a binary conversion engine

name: Spyglass
capability: Minecraft data/resource language server and parser infrastructure using mcdoc schemas for diagnostics, completion and version-aware structured-text analysis.
bestFor: Validating JSON, commands, NBT-like data and resource/data-pack migrations before runtime.
integration: Run target-version validation across changed resources and feed precise diagnostics into Doctor findings and generated migration tests.
currentEvidence: Active organization/repository observed in August 2026.
risks: Schema validation cannot prove gameplay semantics
Version schema selection must be exact

name: NBT Studio
capability: GUI viewer/editor for Java NBT, Java region files, Bedrock little-endian NBT and SNBT with undo/redo, multiselect and format conversion.
bestFor: Human verification of copied worlds, structures and repaired NBT payloads.
integration: Open only copied artifacts after deterministic repair, compare semantic paths, and preserve automated before/after hashes separately.
currentEvidence: Current maintained successor to NBTExplorer with Java and Bedrock support.
risks: Manual edits are not reproducible unless exported as a patch receipt
Region/world changes still require runtime validation

name: Minecraft Repair Brain
capability: Append-only, versioned repair cases covering signatures, exact artifacts, root causes, fixes, failed attempts, supersession, verification and user-confirmed outcomes.
bestFor: Preventing repeated failed repairs and reusing proven fixes only on matching version tuples.
integration: Search before every diagnosis; update the canonical JSONL only after preserving evidence, hashes and applicability.
currentEvidence: Five recovered real repair records were loaded into the v0.8.0 Doctor classifier on 2026-08-20.
risks: Never promote partial static evidence to runtime success
Never overwrite failed or superseded attempts

name: Stonecraft
capability: Versioned Gradle plugin and template that wires Stonecutter and Architectury for multi-version, multi-loader mod projects.
bestFor: Reducing repeated build logic in source-owned Architectury projects.
integration: Generate or migrate in a branch, run all target builds and compare published metadata/artifacts.
currentEvidence: Current repository documentation advertises a maintained plugin and template.
risks: Adds an abstraction layer over two other toolchains
Generated publishing behavior needs target-by-target verification

name: Cloche
capability: Target-oriented cross-platform Minecraft Gradle plugin with source-set separation, data generation, tests, runs, metadata generation and pre-applied Mixin support.
bestFor: Exploring a single-project target model for complex multi-loader/version builds.
integration: Benchmark against loader-native builds in isolated generated projects before adopting.
currentEvidence: Active repository documented in August 2026.
risks: Some debugging/Mixin features are explicitly work in progress
Smaller production evidence base than loader-native tooling

name: Blahaj
capability: Stonecutter-based Gradle plugin for multiversion project setup, dependency declarations, compatibility metadata and publishing.
bestFor: Mining automation ideas and rapidly testing version matrices.
integration: Keep as a research adapter until it passes the Vault cross-version fixture matrix.
currentEvidence: Current repository exists with a fluent multi-platform DSL but limited adoption evidence.
risks: Research-grade maturity
Must not replace proven builds solely for convenience

name: Balm
capability: Common interfaces, events, configs, networking and third-party integrations for Fabric, Forge and NeoForge source mods using loader-native build plugins.
bestFor: Reference architecture or dependency for maintainable source-level loader convergence.
integration: Use as an explicit library dependency in source ports and test every loader artifact separately.
currentEvidence: Battle-tested across a large family of maintained mods.
risks: Not a binary cross-loader bridge
Adds a runtime library dependency

name: Hopper
capability: Platform-aware runtime server-plugin dependency resolution from Hangar, Modrinth, Spiget, GitHub Releases and direct URLs with range/update policies.
bestFor: Designing the Vault server-plugin dependency and update lane.
integration: Borrow provider-resolution and policy ideas; stage downloads and verify hot-load behavior in disposable Paper/Folia/Velocity profiles.
currentEvidence: Current repository documentation covers multiple providers and platform detection.
risks: Runtime hot-loading has platform-specific failure modes
Remote dependency policies require provenance and rollback

name: NeoForm
capability: Creates reproducible and recompilable modern Minecraft sources and adjacent-version patch workspaces.
bestFor: Exact modern game-source reconstruction and tracking upstream changes across releases.
integration: Create isolated patch workspaces, preserve the exact branch/tag/config, apply updates with reject capture, and hash every generated artifact.
currentEvidence: Active NeoForged project; current branches distinguish obfuscated pre-26.1 inputs from unobfuscated Minecraft generations.
risks: Generated game source is reference/build input, not automatically publishable mod source
Branch selection is version-sensitive

name: NeoForm Runtime
capability: Standalone execution-graph CLI for deobfuscation, merging, patching, recompilation, assets and artifact resolution.
bestFor: Deterministic, auditable Minecraft/NeoForge artifact generation outside a full Gradle plugin.
integration: Invoke with pinned NeoForm or NeoForge coordinates, print the graph, redirect every named result, and retain caches/manifests/logs as provenance.
currentEvidence: Actively maintained in the NeoForge toolchain through July 2026.
risks: Large cached artifact graph must be isolated per tuple
Custom repositories and manifests can change reproducibility

name: RetroMCP-Java
capability: Version-profile-driven download, deobfuscation, decompilation, patching, recompilation and reobfuscation for many classic Minecraft versions.
bestFor: Recovering reviewable source and build workspaces for alpha, beta and old release mods.
integration: Select an exact version profile, record mappings/decompiler/patches, build the untouched baseline, then layer port changes with output diffs.
currentEvidence: v1.2 is the current verified release; the project remains the broadest maintained MCP-style legacy reconstruction option found.
risks: Coverage and fidelity differ by historical version
Decompiled source requires ambiguity review

name: RetroFuturaGradle
capability: Modern Gradle replacement for legacy ForgeGradle 1.7.10 development with toolchains, caches, dependency deobfuscation and reliable reobfuscation.
bestFor: Rebuilding and porting source-owned Minecraft 1.7.10 Forge mods.
integration: Generate or migrate an isolated 1.7.10 workspace, build the untouched source, run deobfuscation/reobfuscation checks, and compare output JAR structure.
currentEvidence: 2.0.2 is the latest verified release; 2.0 added Gradle 9 support and a Java 25 build requirement.
risks: Build JVM requirements differ from game runtime requirements
Legacy coremods still require runtime transformer tests

name: RetroFuturaBootstrap
capability: Backwards-compatible LaunchWrapper replacement with ordered compatibility plugins and class/transformer dump diagnostics.
bestFor: Modern-Java legacy runtime bootstrapping and diagnosing early transformer incompatibilities.
integration: Launch disposable profiles with class-dump flags, retain per-transformer outputs, and compare class ordering before and after compatibility plugins.
currentEvidence: Active and used by LWJGL3ify as the early-load foundation.
risks: Bootstrap success does not prove mod behavior
Compatibility plugins can introduce ordering conflicts

name: Cleanroom
capability: Minecraft 1.12.2 loader/runtime continuation with modern Java, LWJGL3, Mixin and compatibility patches.
bestFor: Testing whether 1.12.2 packs can run on modern Java before or alongside source repair.
integration: Create a copied profile, install exact Cleanroom/Fugue versions, run client/server/world/restart matrices, and store mod-by-mod compatibility evidence.
currentEvidence: Active CleanroomMC project in July-August 2026; README advertises Java 25+ and LWJGL3.

Coremods and graphics mods need dedicated coverage

name: MixinBooter
capability: Unified Mixin configuration discovery, CleanMix/MixinExtras integration and dedicated diagnostics for 1.8-1.12.2.
bestFor: Porting or stabilizing Mixin-heavy legacy Forge mods and resolving competing Mixin loaders.

currentEvidence: Current 11.x line uses CleanMix and supports 1.8 through 1.12.2.

capability: Modular compatibility layer combining legacy Mixin loader features without forcing one monolithic provider.
bestFor: Minecraft 1.7.10 Mixin compatibility and selected 1.8.9-1.12.2 cases.
integration: Resolve required modules from artifact metadata, reject duplicate providers, and execute the project's published compatibility fixtures plus pack-specific tests.
currentEvidence: 0.3.1 released 2026-05-27 with signed release assets and an ASM remapper fix.
risks: Module overlap must be solved explicitly
Partial support above 1.7.10 requires tuple-specific proof

name: LWJGL3ify
capability: LWJGL2-to-LWJGL3 compatibility, modern-Java bootstrap, native/runtime replacement and targeted ASM/Mixin fixes for 1.7.10.
bestFor: Modernizing the runtime environment of large 1.7.10 packs without pretending the mods were source-ported.

currentEvidence: Active current line documents modern Java and bundles RetroFuturaBootstrap.

capability: Targeted Cleanroom-era compatibility patches for mods that otherwise fail on modern Java or the revised 1.12.2 runtime.
bestFor: Known per-mod fixes after a Cleanroom baseline identifies exact failures.
integration: Match exact mod/version tuples, enable only applicable patches, and verify the original reproducer plus regression paths.
currentEvidence: Repository was actively pushed on 2026-08-12.
risks: Patch coverage is finite and version-sensitive
A compatibility patch can hide a deeper semantic break

name: PaperMC DataConverter
capability: High-performance rewrite of Minecraft data conversion with explicit walkers and debuggable conversion code.
bestFor: Researching faster conversion architecture, diffing vanilla schema behavior and constructing focused data fixtures.

name: Mod Publish Plugin
capability: Gradle artifact publication to common Minecraft destinations with configuration-cache support.
